objects.description: Represents a single UPnP SOAP method argument, pairing an element (argument) name with its string value. Used when invoking UPnP actions via simpleUPnPcommand().

Holds resolved, absolute URLs for key IGD services and the root description, built from a device’s root description. Buffers are allocated and later freed by the library. Use GetUPNPUrls() to initialize and FreeUPNPUrls() to release.

Opaque forward-declared structure representing the parsed list of port mappings returned by UPNP_GetListOfPortMappings(). Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the actual definition lives elsewhere in the miniupnpc library. Treat it as an opaque handle passed to and filled by API functions that operate on port-mapping lists. Details of its fields and lifetime management are unknown from this header.

objects.definition:
typedef enum { PortMappingEltNone,
       PortMappingEntry, NewRemoteHost,
       NewExternalPort, NewProtocol,
       NewInternalPort, NewInternalClient,
       NewEnabled, NewDescription,
       NewLeaseTime } portMappingElt;
objects.description: Enumeration of XML element identifiers used while parsing the GetListOfPortMappings response. Values distinguish the different tags inside a PortMappingEntry. Exact integer values follow the order listed starting at 0.

objects.definition:
struct PortMapping {
	struct PortMapping * l_next;	/* next list element */
	UNSIGNED_INTEGER leaseTime;	/* in seconds */
	unsigned short externalPort;	/* external port */
	unsigned short internalPort;	/* internal port */
	char remoteHost[64];	/* empty for wildcard */
	char internalClient[64];	/* internal IP address */
	char description[64];	/* description */
	char protocol[4];		/* `TCP` or `UDP` */
	unsigned char enabled;	/* 0 (false) or 1 (true) */
};
objects.description: Node of a singly linked list describing one port mapping entry returned by GetListOfPortMappings. Holds ports, protocol, client, lease time, enabled flag, and description. The protocol field is a short string (e.g., "TCP" or "UDP"). The l_next field links to the next PortMapping.

Parsing context and result container for ParsePortListing(). l_head points to the head of the linked list of PortMapping nodes produced by the parser; curelt tracks the current XML element during parsing.

Holds the parsed endpoint URLs and service type for a single UPnP Internet Gateway Device service (control URL, event subscription URL, SCPD URL). Used while parsing a device description XML and as embedded fields in IGDdatas.

Aggregates parsing state and extracted data from a UPnP IGD device description XML. Includes base/presentation URLs, current XML element and depth, plus captured service descriptors for WANCommonInterfaceConfig, WANIP/PPPConnection (first/second), WANIPv6FirewallControl, and a temporary slot used during parsing.

Forward-declared internal linked-list node used to hold name/value pairs while parsing. Not exposed publicly; only referenced as a pointer within NameValueParserData. Full definition is not present in this header.

Holds state and results for parsing UPnP SOAP/XML replies: a linked list of name/value pairs, the current element name buffer, optional port listing buffer and length, and pointers/length for the current character data. Instances are filled by ParseNameValue() and should be cleaned with ClearNameValueList().

Pointer type corresponding to the function’s return type (const char *). Note: This header does not define any custom data types (no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes). It only declares the function strupnperror. This entry is included solely to acknowledge that no user-defined types are present; there is no standalone type definition for const char * in this header.

Intrusive singly linked-list node representing a discovered UPnP device. Fields include the next-node pointer (pNext), the device description URL (descURL), the service type string (st), the unique service name (usn), and the IPv6 scope identifier (scope_id). The trailing buffer is a flexible/hack array intended to store contiguous string data for descURL, st, and usn to minimize allocations. Construction details are not provided in this header; lists are typically obtained from discovery APIs and must be freed with freeUPNPDevlist().

No custom types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The header only declares two functions (miniwget and miniwget_getaddr) that operate on standard C types and void pointers. Therefore, there is no user-defined data type to document.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. The file only defines the MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC macro for symbol visibility/export on different platforms.

functions.name: simpleUPnPcommand
functions.signature: char * simpleUPnPcommand(const char * url, const char * service, const char * action, const struct UPNParg * args, int * bufsize);
functions.description: Execute a UPnP SOAP action against the given control URL and service. Returns the raw XML response buffer and outputs its size via bufsize, or NULL on error. Intended for low-level/direct SOAP method invocation.
requirements: url must be a valid, reachable control URL for the target service.
service must name the target UPnP service (e.g., WANIPConnection).
action must be the SOAP action name to invoke on the service.
args is a list of UPnP arguments; termination/ownership semantics are not specified in this header (unknown: consult library documentation).
bufsize should be a valid, non-NULL pointer if the caller needs the returned buffer size; it is set only on success.
On error, the function returns NULL (caller must handle NULL).
Ownership/lifetime of the returned buffer is not explicitly documented here; likely dynamically allocated and must be freed by the caller (unknown: confirm in library docs).
Error reporting is minimal as noted in the header (caller should not rely on detailed error codes).

functions.name: upnpDiscover
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC struct UPNPDev * upnpDiscover(int delay, const char * multicastif, const char * minissdpdsock, int localport, int ipv6, unsigned char ttl, int * error);
functions.description: Discover UPnP IGD devices on the local network via SSDP. Returns a linked list of discovered devices or NULL on error/timeouts. Intended as the standard IGD discovery entry point.
requirements: delay is the maximum wait time in milliseconds for device responses; must be >= 0.
multicastif may be NULL to use the default multicast interface; otherwise must be a valid interface identifier/name.
minissdpdsock may be NULL to use the default MiniSSDPd socket; otherwise must be a valid path to a MiniSSDPd socket.
localport selects the UDP source port: use UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_SAME for 1900, UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_ANY to let the system assign, or a specific port number.
ipv6 must be 0 for IPv4 discovery or 1 for IPv6 discovery.
ttl is the IP multicast TTL; UDA 1.1 advises default 2.
error, if non-NULL, receives an error code when NULL is returned; caller must check when return is NULL.
On success, the caller must free the returned list using freeUPNPDevlist().

functions.name: upnpDiscoverAll
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC struct UPNPDev * upnpDiscoverAll(int delay, const char * multicastif, const char * minissdpdsock, int localport, int ipv6, unsigned char ttl, int * error);
functions.description: Discover all UPnP devices (search target "ssdp:all"). Returns a linked list of all discovered devices or NULL on error.
requirements: delay is the maximum wait time in milliseconds; must be >= 0.
multicastif may be NULL to use the default multicast interface; otherwise must be valid.
minissdpdsock may be NULL to use default; otherwise must be a valid MiniSSDPd socket path.
localport selects the UDP source port: UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_SAME, UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_ANY, or a specific port number.
ipv6 must be 0 (IPv4) or 1 (IPv6).
ttl should typically be 2 as advised by UDA 1.1.
error, if non-NULL, is set when the function returns NULL.
On success, the caller must free the returned list using freeUPNPDevlist().

functions.name: upnpDiscoverDevice
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC struct UPNPDev * upnpDiscoverDevice(const char * device, int delay, const char * multicastif, const char * minissdpdsock, int localport, int ipv6, unsigned char ttl, int * error);
functions.description: Discover UPnP devices of a specific type (search target equals the provided device type). Returns a linked list of matching devices or NULL on error/none found.
requirements: device must be a valid UPnP device type string (e.g., "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:InternetGatewayDevice:1").
delay is the maximum wait time in milliseconds; must be >= 0.
multicastif may be NULL to use the default multicast interface; otherwise must be valid.
minissdpdsock may be NULL to use default; otherwise must be a valid MiniSSDPd socket path.
localport selects the UDP source port: UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_SAME, UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_ANY, or a specific port number.
ipv6 must be 0 (IPv4) or 1 (IPv6).
ttl should typically be 2 as advised by UDA 1.1.
error, if non-NULL, is set when the function returns NULL.
On success, the caller must free the returned list using freeUPNPDevlist().

functions.name: upnpDiscoverDevices
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC struct UPNPDev * upnpDiscoverDevices(const char * const deviceTypes[], int delay, const char * multicastif, const char * minissdpdsock, int localport, int ipv6, unsigned char ttl, int * error, int searchalltypes);
functions.description: Discover one or several UPnP device types. Returns a linked list of discovered devices or NULL on error/none found. Can stop at the first type with results or search all types.
requirements: deviceTypes must be a NULL-terminated array of device type strings; the last entry must be NULL.
delay is the maximum wait time in milliseconds; must be >= 0.
multicastif may be NULL to use the default multicast interface; otherwise must be valid.
minissdpdsock may be NULL to use default; otherwise must be a valid MiniSSDPd socket path.
localport selects the UDP source port: UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_SAME, UPNP_LOCAL_PORT_ANY, or a specific port number.
ipv6 must be 0 (IPv4) or 1 (IPv6).
ttl should typically be 2 as advised by UDA 1.1.
error, if non-NULL, is set when the function returns NULL.
searchalltypes: set to 0 to stop on the first type returning results; non-zero to search all types.
On success, the caller must free the returned list using freeUPNPDevlist().

functions.name: parserootdesc
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC void parserootdesc(const char * buffer, int bufsize, struct IGDdatas * data);
functions.description: Parse the root XML device description and populate the provided IGDdatas structure for quick access to relevant IGD information.
requirements: buffer must point to a memory region containing the device root XML description.
bufsize is the size in bytes of buffer and must match the actual buffer length; must be >= 0.
data must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an IGDdatas structure to be filled.
Caller must ensure the buffer remains valid for the duration of parsing.

functions.name: UPNP_GetValidIGD
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetValidIGD(struct UPNPDev * devlist, struct UPNPUrls * urls, struct IGDdatas * data, char * lanaddr, int lanaddrlen, char * wanaddr, int wanaddrlen);
functions.description: Scan the discovered device list for a valid (and possibly connected) IGD, and fill URLs, IGD data, and local/public addresses. Returns a status code indicating the IGD state (e.g., connected, private IP, disconnected, unknown).
requirements: devlist must be a device list obtained from upnpDiscover(), upnpDiscoverAll(), upnpDiscoverDevice(), or upnpDiscoverDevices().
urls must be a valid pointer; on any non-zero return value it is initialized and must later be freed with FreeUPNPUrls(urls).
data must be a valid pointer; on any non-zero return value it is populated.
lanaddr must be a writable buffer with size lanaddrlen to receive the local address; lanaddrlen must reflect the buffer size.
wanaddr must be a writable buffer with size wanaddrlen to receive the public address; wanaddrlen must reflect the buffer size.
The return value is one of: UPNP_NO_IGD, UPNP_CONNECTED_IGD, UPNP_PRIVATEIP_IGD, UPNP_DISCONNECTED_IGD, or UPNP_UNKNOWN_DEVICE; caller must handle each case appropriately.
Caller must invoke FreeUPNPUrls(urls) after use to free allocated memory when urls has been set.

functions.name: UPNP_GetIGDFromUrl
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetIGDFromUrl(const char * rootdescurl, struct UPNPUrls * urls, struct IGDdatas * data, char * lanaddr, int lanaddrlen);
functions.description: Initialize IGD URLs and data directly from a known root description URL, bypassing the discovery phase. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: rootdescurl must be a valid, reachable root device description URL.
urls must be a valid pointer; on success it is initialized and must be freed with FreeUPNPUrls(urls).
data must be a valid pointer; on success it is populated.
lanaddr must be a writable buffer with size lanaddrlen to receive the local address; lanaddrlen must reflect the buffer size.
Return value semantics: 0 means not OK; 1 means OK; caller must check and handle failure.
Caller must invoke FreeUPNPUrls(urls) after use when initialized.

functions.name: GetUPNPUrls
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC void GetUPNPUrls(struct UPNPUrls * urls, struct IGDdatas * data, const char * descURL, unsigned int scope_id);
functions.description: Prepare and resolve absolute service/control URLs from the device root description and IGD data. Optionally add IPv6 scope ID to link-local addresses.
requirements: urls must be a valid pointer to a UPNPUrls structure to initialize; its members will be allocated/filled.
data must be a valid IGDdatas pointer populated from the device description (e.g., via parserootdesc/UPNP_GetValidIGD).
descURL must be the root description URL for the device.
scope_id, if non-zero, is appended as an IPv6 scope to link-local URLs; set to 0 if not needed.
After use, the caller must free and zero URLs with FreeUPNPUrls(urls).

functions.name: FreeUPNPUrls
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC void FreeUPNPUrls(struct UPNPUrls * urls);
functions.description: Free and zero all dynamically allocated members inside a UPNPUrls structure after they were prepared/initialized for use.
requirements: urls must be a valid pointer previously initialized by GetUPNPUrls() or UPNP_GetValidIGD()/UPNP_GetIGDFromUrl().
After calling, the URL buffers are freed and zeroed; the urls pointer itself is not freed (only its members).
Caller must not use the freed URL strings after this call.

functions.name: UPNPIGD_IsConnected
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNPIGD_IsConnected(struct UPNPUrls * urls, struct IGDdatas * data);
functions.description: Check whether the IGD reports an active/connected WAN status. Internally uses UPNP_GetStatusInfo(). Returns 1 if connected, 0 if disconnected.
requirements: urls must be initialized IGD URLs (e.g., via GetUPNPUrls or UPNP_GetValidIGD).
data must be the corresponding IGD data structure for the same device.
Caller must handle the binary return value (1 connected, 0 disconnected).

functions.name: UPNP_GetTotalBytesSent
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC UNSIGNED_INTEGER UPNP_GetTotalBytesSent(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype);
functions.description: Queries WANCommonInterfaceConfig:GetTotalBytesSent. Returns a 32-bit unsigned counter of bytes sent on the WAN interface. Counter rolls over to 0 on overflow.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANCommonInterfaceConfig service of a WANDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANCommonInterfaceConfig:1.
Return value is a 32-bit unsigned counter and may wrap to 0 after reaching max.

functions.name: UPNP_GetTotalBytesReceived
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC UNSIGNED_INTEGER UPNP_GetTotalBytesReceived(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype);
functions.description: Queries WANCommonInterfaceConfig:GetTotalBytesReceived. Returns a 32-bit unsigned counter of bytes received on the WAN interface. Counter rolls over to 0 on overflow.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANCommonInterfaceConfig service of a WANDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANCommonInterfaceConfig:1.
Return value is a 32-bit unsigned counter and may wrap to 0 after reaching max.

functions.name: UPNP_GetTotalPacketsSent
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC UNSIGNED_INTEGER UPNP_GetTotalPacketsSent(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype);
functions.description: Queries WANCommonInterfaceConfig:GetTotalPacketsSent. Returns a 32-bit unsigned counter of packets sent on the WAN interface. Counter rolls over to 0 on overflow.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANCommonInterfaceConfig service of a WANDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANCommonInterfaceConfig:1.
Return value is a 32-bit unsigned counter and may wrap to 0 after reaching max.

functions.name: UPNP_GetTotalPacketsReceived
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC UNSIGNED_INTEGER UPNP_GetTotalPacketsReceived(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype);
functions.description: Queries WANCommonInterfaceConfig:GetTotalPacketsReceived. Returns a 32-bit unsigned counter of packets received on the WAN interface. Counter rolls over to 0 on overflow.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANCommonInterfaceConfig service of a WANDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANCommonInterfaceConfig:1.
Return value is a 32-bit unsigned counter and may wrap to 0 after reaching max.

functions.name: UPNP_GetStatusInfo
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetStatusInfo(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, char * status, unsigned int * uptime, char * lastconnerror);
functions.description: Calls WANIPConnection:GetStatusInfo to retrieve connection status, uptime, and last connection error.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
status must point to a writable buffer of at least 64 bytes and will contain one of: Unconfigured, Connecting, Connected, PendingDisconnect, Disconnecting, Disconnected.
uptime must be a valid pointer; output is time in seconds.

lastconnerror must point to a writable buffer of at least 64 bytes and will contain one of: ERROR_NONE, ERROR_COMMAND_ABORTED, ERROR_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_INTERNET, ERROR_USER_DISCONNECT, ERROR_ISP_DISCONNECT, ERROR_IDLE_DISCONNECT, ERROR_FORCED_DISCONNECT, ERROR_NO_CARRIER, ERROR_IP_CONFIGURATION, ERROR_UNKNOWN.
Function returns UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR, or a UPnP error code.

functions.name: UPNP_GetConnectionTypeInfo
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetConnectionTypeInfo(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, char * connectionType);
functions.description: Calls WANIPConnection:GetConnectionTypeInfo to obtain the WAN connection type.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
connectionType must point to a writable buffer of at least 64 bytes and will contain one of: Unconfigured, IP_Routed, IP_Bridged.
Returns UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR, or a UPnP error code.

functions.name: UPNP_GetExternalIPAddress
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetExternalIPAddress(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, char * extIpAdd);
functions.description: Calls WANIPConnection:GetExternalIPAddress to retrieve the current external IPv4 address.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
extIpAdd must point to a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.

May return UPnP errors 402 (Invalid Args) or 501 (Action Failed). Also may return UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_HTTP_ERROR, or an UPnP error code.

functions.name: UPNP_GetLinkLayerMaxBitRates
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetLinkLayerMaxBitRates(const char* controlURL, const char* servicetype, unsigned int * bitrateDown, unsigned int * bitrateUp);
functions.description: Calls WANCommonInterfaceConfig:GetCommonLinkProperties to retrieve downstream and upstream max bit rates (bps).
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANCommonInterfaceConfig service of a WANDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANCommonInterfaceConfig:1.
bitrateDown must be a valid pointer; output is bits per second.
bitrateUp must be a valid pointer; output is bits per second.
Returns UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR, or a UPnP error code.

functions.name: UPNP_AddPortMapping
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_AddPortMapping(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, const char * extPort, const char * inPort, const char * inClient, const char * desc, const char * proto, const char * remoteHost, const char * leaseDuration);
functions.description: Calls WANIPConnection:AddPortMapping to create a port forwarding (TCP/UDP) entry.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
extPort must be the external port (string).
inPort must be the internal port (string).
inClient must be the internal client IP address (string).
desc may be NULL (defaults to "libminiupnpc"); otherwise string description.
proto must be "TCP" or "UDP".
remoteHost should be an IP or empty string for wildcard; most IGDs don't support non-wildcard.
leaseDuration must be a string between 0 and 604800 (inclusive).

Possible UPnP errors include: 402, 501, 606, 715, 716, 718, 724, 725, 726, 727, 728, 729, 732. Function may also return UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_MEM_ALLOC_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_HTTP_ERROR, or UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR.

functions.name: UPNP_AddAnyPortMapping
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_AddAnyPortMapping(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, const char * extPort, const char * inPort, const char * inClient, const char * desc, const char * proto, const char * remoteHost, const char * leaseDuration, char * reservedPort);
functions.description: WANIPConnection:2 AddAnyPortMapping variant. Requests a port mapping; device may assign a different external port, returned in reservedPort.
requirements: Available only for WANIPConnection:2.
controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:2.
extPort, inPort, inClient, desc (or NULL for default), proto ("TCP" or "UDP"), remoteHost (IP or empty for wildcard), leaseDuration as strings, same semantics as AddPortMapping.
reservedPort must point to a writable buffer of at least 6 bytes to receive the assigned external port.

Possible UPnP errors include: 402, 501, 606, 715, 716, 728, 729, 732. Function may also return UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_MEM_ALLOC_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_HTTP_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_RESPONSE, or UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR.

functions.name: UPNP_DeletePortMapping
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_DeletePortMapping(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, const char * extPort, const char * proto, const char * remoteHost);
functions.description: Calls WANIPConnection:DeletePortMapping to remove a specific port mapping.
requirements: Use the same argument values used when creating the mapping via UPNP_AddPortMapping.
controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
extPort is the external port (string).
proto must be "TCP" or "UDP".
remoteHost must be the IP or empty string for wildcard; most IGDs don't support non-wildcard.
Possible UPnP errors: 402, 606, 714. Function may also return UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_MEM_ALLOC_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_HTTP_ERROR, or UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR.

functions.name: UPNP_DeletePortMappingRange
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_DeletePortMappingRange(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, const char * extPortStart, const char * extPortEnd, const char * proto, const char * manage);
functions.description: WANIPConnection:2 DeletePortMappingRange to remove port mappings in a specified external port range.
requirements: Available only for WANIPConnection:2.
Use argument conventions consistent with AddPortMapping; remoteHost is usually not supported and not present here.
controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:2.
extPortStart and extPortEnd are the external port range bounds (strings).
proto must be "TCP" or "UDP".
manage must be "0" to remove only this IGD's mappings or "1" to also remove for other clients.
Possible UPnP errors: 606, 730, 733. Function may also return UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_MEM_ALLOC_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_HTTP_ERROR, or UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR.

functions.name: UPNP_GetPortMappingNumberOfEntries
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetPortMappingNumberOfEntries(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, unsigned int * numEntries);
functions.description: Calls WANIPConnection:GetPortMappingNumberOfEntries to get the count of existing port mappings (not supported by all routers).
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
numEntries must be a valid pointer to receive the count.
May return UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_HTTP_ERROR, UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR, or a UPnP error code.

functions.name: UPNP_GetSpecificPortMappingEntry
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetSpecificPortMappingEntry(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, const char * extPort, const char * proto, const char * remoteHost, char * intClient, char * intPort, char * desc, char * enabled, char * leaseDuration);
functions.description: Retrieves details of a specific port mapping identified by external port, protocol, and remoteHost.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
extPort is the external port (string).
proto must be "TCP" or "UDP".
remoteHost must be IP or empty string for wildcard; most IGDs don't support non-wildcard.
intClient must be a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
intPort must be a writable buffer of at least 6 bytes.
desc must be a writable buffer of at least 80 bytes.
enabled must be a writable buffer of at least 4 bytes.
leaseDuration must be a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
Possible UPnP errors: 402, 501, 606, 714. Returns UPNPCOMMAND_SUCCESS, UPNPCOMMAND_INVALID_ARGS, UPNPCOMMAND_UNKNOWN_ERROR, or a UPnP error code.

functions.name: UPNP_GetSpecificPortMappingEntryExt
functions.signature: MINIUPNP_LIBSPEC int UPNP_GetSpecificPortMappingEntryExt(const char * controlURL, const char * servicetype, const char * extPort, const char * proto, const char * remoteHost, char * intClient, char * intPort, char * desc, size_t desclen, char * enabled, char * leaseDuration);
functions.description: Extended version of GetSpecificPortMappingEntry with caller-provided desc buffer length.
requirements: controlURL must refer to a WANIPConnection service of a WANConnectionDevice.
servicetype must be urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1.
extPort is the external port (string).
proto must be "TCP" or "UDP".
remoteHost must be IP or empty string for wildcard; most IGDs don't support non-wildcard.
intClient must be a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
intPort must be a writable buffer of at least 6 bytes.
desc must be a writable buffer of length desclen; desclen must specify the actual desc buffer size.

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for UPnP IGD device description XML (root device)
# Target stubs consume this as FUZZ_PARAM_STR for parserootdesc() and GetUPNPUrls()
# We aim to produce valid, self-consistent IGD descriptions with varying structures.

XML_DECL = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>\n'

def rnd_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(0, len(items))]

def maybe(rng: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return rng.random() < p

def xml_escape(s: str) -> str:
    return (s.replace('&', '&')
             .replace('<', '<')
             .replace('>', '>')
             .replace('"', '"')
             .replace("'", '''))

# Build a consistent set of base URL and paths for services
def build_urls(rng: random.Random, ipv6: bool) -> Tuple[str, str, str, str, str]:
    # Return: (urlBase, presURL, cif_control, wanip1_control, wanppp1_control)
    hostnames = [
        "192.168.%d.%d" % (rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(1, 254)),
        "router.local",
        "gateway.home",
    ]
    if ipv6:
        # generate a link-local-like address without zone index; scope_id may be added by library
        hextet = lambda: format(rng.randrange(0, 0xffff), 'x')
        hostnames.append("fe80::%s:%s:%s:%s" % (hextet(), hextet(), hextet(), hextet()))

    host = rnd_choice(rng, hostnames)
    scheme = "http"
    port = rng.choice([80, 52869, 5000, 1780])
    base_path = "/igd/" + str(rng.randrange(1, 100)) + "/"
    urlbase = f"{scheme}://{host}:{port}{base_path}"
    pres = urlbase + "present.html"
    # Service control paths
    cif_ctrl = urlbase + "ctl/CIF"
    wanip_ctrl = urlbase + "ctl/WANIPConn"
    wanppp_ctrl = urlbase + "ctl/WANPPPConn"
    return urlbase, pres, cif_ctrl, wanip_ctrl, wanppp_ctrl

# Build a single service entry block
def service_block(service_type: str, control_url: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For variety, sometimes provide relative URLs to exercise URLBase joining
    def maybe_rel(url: str) -> str:
        if maybe(rng, 0.5):
            # make it relative to the base path
            return "/" + url.split('/', 3)[-1] if "/" in url else url
        return url
    scpd = control_url.rsplit('/', 1)[0] + "/scpd.xml"

        f"        <serviceId>urn:upnp-org:serviceId:{xml_escape(service_type.split(':')[-2])}</serviceId>\n"
        f"        <SCPDURL>{xml_escape(maybe_rel(scpd))}</SCPDURL>\n"

def gen_udn(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    hexs = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(32))
    return f"uuid:{hexs[:8]}-{hexs[8:12]}-{hexs[12:16]}-{hexs[16:20]}-{hexs[20:32]}"

def device_block(urlbase: str, presurl: str, cif_ctrl: str, wanip_ctrl: str, wanppp_ctrl: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose whether we present WANIPConnection:1 or WANPPPConnection:1 (or both)

    # Optionally include a second WANConnectionDevice with another service to exercise 'second'
    second_services = ""
    if maybe(rng, 0.5):

        second_services = (
            "      <serviceList>\n" +

    dev = []
    dev.append("    <device>\n")

    dev.append(f"      <presentationURL>{xml_escape(presurl)}</presentationURL>\n")
    dev.append("      <deviceList>\n")
    # Embed a WANDevice with a WANConnectionDevice inside, as typical IGD structure
    dev.append("        <device>\n")
    dev.append("          <deviceType>urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:WANDevice:1</deviceType>\n")
    dev.append("          <serviceList>\n")
    dev.append(service_block("urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANCommonInterfaceConfig:1", cif_ctrl, rng))
    dev.append("          </serviceList>\n")
    dev.append("          <deviceList>\n")
    dev.append("            <device>\n")
    dev.append("              <deviceType>urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:WANConnectionDevice:1</deviceType>\n")
    dev.append("              <serviceList>\n")
    dev.extend(services)
    dev.append("              </serviceList>\n")

        dev.append("                <device>\n")
        dev.append("                  <deviceType>urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:WANConnectionDevice:1</deviceType>\n")
        dev.append(second_services)
        dev.append("                </device>\n")
        dev.append("              </deviceList>\n")
    dev.append("            </device>\n")
    dev.append("          </deviceList>\n")
    dev.append("        </device>\n")
    dev.append("      </deviceList>\n")
    dev.append("    </device>\n")
    return ''.join(dev)

def build_root_xml(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    ipv6 = maybe(rng, 0.4)
    urlbase, pres, cif, wanip, wanppp = build_urls(rng, ipv6)

    # Sometimes omit URLBase to test resolution from descURL; but for GetUPNPUrls the fuzzer passes descURL separately.
    include_urlbase = maybe(rng, 0.7)

    # Namespace variations to exercise parser tolerance
    ns_upnp = rnd_choice(rng, [
        "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device-1-0",
        "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device-1-1",
        "urn:schemas-upnp-org:device-2-0",
    ])
    ns_dlna = "urn:schemas-dlna-org:device-1-0"

    header = [XML_DECL]
    header.append(f"<root xmlns=\"{ns_upnp}\" xmlns:dlna=\"{ns_dlna}\">\n")
    if include_urlbase:
        header.append(f"  <URLBase>{xml_escape(urlbase)}</URLBase>\n")
    header.append("  <specVersion><major>1</major><minor>0</minor></specVersion>\n")

    body = device_block(urlbase, pres, cif, wanip, wanppp, rng)

    footer = ["</root>\n"]

    return ''.join(header) + body + ''.join(footer)

# Generate a plausible description URL for GetUPNPUrls callers
def build_desc_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Match scheme/host patterns used above
    ipv6 = maybe(rng, 0.3)
    urlbase, _, _, _, _ = build_urls(rng, ipv6)
    # Root description typically ends with rootDesc.xml or root.xml
    tail = rnd_choice(rng, ["rootDesc.xml", "root.xml", "desc.xml"])
    return urlbase + tail

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide which buffer the fuzz stub is likely to request first; both parserootdesc and GetUPNPUrls use FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # We prioritize returning a valid XML root description as bytes.
    xml = build_root_xml(rng)

    # Constrain size to <= 4096 bytes; if larger, lightly vary by trimming optional whitespace
    b = xml.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Simple truncation at a safe boundary: ensure we end with closing root
        # Rebuild with less nested content
        rng2 = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5)
        ipv6 = False
        urlbase, pres, cif, wanip, wanppp = build_urls(rng2, ipv6)
        minimal = (
            XML_DECL +
            f"<root xmlns=\"urn:schemas-upnp-org:device-1-0\">\n" +
            f"  <URLBase>{xml_escape(urlbase)}</URLBase>\n" +
            "  <specVersion><major>1</major><minor>0</minor></specVersion>\n" +
            device_block(urlbase, pres, cif, wanip, wanppp, rng2) +
            "</root>\n"
        )
        b = minimal.encode('utf-8')
    return b[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid/interesting URL strings for miniupnpc GetUPNPUrls-related fuzzers.
# We focus on producing plausible root description URLs and variants with IPv4/IPv6,
# ports, paths, URLBase quirks, and optional scope_id placeholders.

SCHEMES = [
    "http",
]

HOSTS_IPV4 = [
    "192.168.0.1",
    "192.168.1.1",
    "10.0.0.1",
    "172.16.0.1",
    "127.0.0.1",
]

# Link-local with zone id placeholder (scope will be provided separately by fuzzer via scope_id)
HOSTS_IPV6 = [
    "[fe80::1]",
    "[fe80::1234:5678:abcd]",
    "[::1]",
    "[2001:db8::1]",
]

DOMAINS = [
    "router.local",
    "igd.home",
    "example.com",
]

# Common UPnP description paths
DESC_PATHS = [
    "/rootDesc.xml",
    "/rootdesc.xml",
    "/rootDesc",
    "/upnp/rootdesc.xml",
    "/upnp/igd.xml",
    "/igd.xml",
    "/udesc.xml",
]

# Extra parameters that some devices accept, benign for HTTP GET
QUERY_PARAMS = [
    "",  # no query
    "?v=1",
    "?lang=en",
    "?cache=0",
    "?udn=uuid:device-1",
]

PORTS = [80, 1900, 5000, 8080, 49152, 49153, 65535]

# Some path oddities that parsers may normalize
PATH_VARIANTS = [
    "",
    "/",
    "/./",
    "/../../",
]

USERINFO = [
    "",
    "admin:@",
    "user:pass@",
]


def _rand(r: random.Random):
    return r


def rand_choice(r: random.Random, arr: List[str]):
    return arr[r.randrange(len(arr))]


def make_host(r: random.Random) -> str:
    kind = r.choice(["ipv4", "ipv6", "domain"])
    if kind == "ipv4":
        return r.choice(HOSTS_IPV4)
    if kind == "ipv6":
        # Occasionally add a zone id placeholder in the host (ignored by HTTP libs but seen in URLs)
        base = r.choice(HOSTS_IPV6)
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            # Insert a scope hint like %25eth0 or %251
            zone = r.choice(["eth0", "en0", "1", "2"])  # percent-encoded %
            return base[:-1] + f"%25{zone}]"
        return base
    # domain
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # Create a subdomain chain
        sub = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(r.randint(3,6)))
        return f"{sub}." + r.choice(DOMAINS)
    return r.choice(DOMAINS)


def make_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(DESC_PATHS)
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        # Prepend some path variants
        pref = r.choice(PATH_VARIANTS)
        # Avoid doubling slashes badly
        if pref.endswith('/') and base.startswith('/'):
            base2 = pref[:-1] + base
        else:
            base2 = pref + base
    else:
        base2 = base
    # Occasionally append extra segments
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        segs = ["desc", "device", "xml", "upnp", "igd"]
        extra = "/" + "/".join(r.choice(segs) for _ in range(r.randint(1,2)))
        if not base2.endswith('/') and not extra.startswith('/'):
            base2 += "/"
        base2 += extra
    return base2


def make_query(r: random.Random) -> str:
    q = r.choice(QUERY_PARAMS)
    if q and r.random() < 0.3:
        # add another benign param
        key = r.choice(["ver", "ts", "guid", "sid"]) 
        val = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(4,8)))
        sep = '&' if '?' in q else '?'
        q += f"{sep}{key}={val}"
    return q


def make_url(r: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = r.choice(SCHEMES)
    userinfo = r.choice(USERINFO)
    host = make_host(r)
    # Optionally add a port
    port = ''
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        portnum = r.choice(PORTS)
        # Avoid wrapping brackets incorrectly for IPv6 (brackets already in host)
        port = f":{portnum}"
    # Build authority
    authority = f"{userinfo}{host}{port}"
    # Path and query
    path = make_path(r)
    query = make_query(r)
    # Occasionally append a fragment (ignored by HTTP), can exercise URL parsing code that copies strings
    frag = ''
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        frag = '#sec1'
    return f"{scheme}://{authority}{path}{query}{frag}"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Mix in some variability across calls with same seed by stepping RNG a few times
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 7)):
        r.random()

    # Choose a strategy:
    #  - 0: Plain IPv4 rootdesc URL
    #  - 1: IPv6 link-local with zone id hint
    #  - 2: Domain-based with userinfo
    #  - 3: Edge path/queries
    strategy = r.randrange(4)

    urls: List[str] = []

    if strategy == 0:
        # Multiple common IPv4 endpoints
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
            host = r.choice(HOSTS_IPV4)
            port = r.choice([80, 1900, 5000, 8080])
            path = r.choice(DESC_PATHS)
            q = r.choice(["", "?v=1", "?cache=0"]) 
            urls.append(f"http://{host}:{port}{path}{q}")
    elif strategy == 1:
        # IPv6 with optional zone id and various ports
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
            host = make_host(r)
            port = r.choice(PORTS)
            urls.append(f"http://{host}:{port}{make_path(r)}{make_query(r)}")
    elif strategy == 2:
        # Domains with and without userinfo
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
            ui = r.choice(USERINFO)
            dom = r.choice(DOMAINS)
            port = ":" + str(r.choice(PORTS)) if r.random() < 0.8 else ""
            urls.append(f"http://{ui}{dom}{port}{make_path(r)}{make_query(r)}")
    else:
        # Diverse fully randomized URLs using builder
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
            urls.append(make_url(r))

    # Join multiple URLs with newlines so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can consume as one or split
    payload = "\n".join(urls)

    # Ensure size limit
    b = payload.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
    return b

import random
import ipaddress
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid ASCII buffers intended to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# within the UPNP_AddPortMapping / UPNP_AddAnyPortMapping fuzzers. Those stubs use
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - inClient: an IPv4 address string (preferred valid dotted-quad)
# - desc: a short description (<=63 chars) or may be NULL (the stub decides)
# - remoteHost: either empty string or arbitrary hostname/IP (<=63 chars)
# The fuzzers also need urls->controlURL to be non-NULL. That comes from the harness,
# not from this buffer. Our goal is to pack multiple strings into one bytes buffer so
# that the harness can slice them as FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls out strings sequentially.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a sequence of NUL-terminated strings in this order:
#   1) inClient: valid IPv4 dotted-quad
#   2) desc: plausible short description (ASCII, <= 63 chars)
#   3) remoteHost: either empty string or hostname/IP (ASCII, <= 63)
#   4) extra variants to feed further FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls if present
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Ensure variability with seed while remaining valid.
#
# Helper generation functions below intentionally produce valid values.

COMMON_HOST_LABELS = [
    "router", "gateway", "home", "office", "srv", "wan", "lan", "gw", "edge",
    "fw", "nat", "upnp", "igd", "box"
]

COMMON_TLDS = ["local", "lan", "home", "invalid", "example", "test", "corp", "net", "com"]

DESC_WORDS = [
    "Auto", "UPnP", "Mapping", "Service", "Test", "Fuzz", "MiniUPnPc", "Client",
    "Game", "Web", "SSH", "RDP", "VPN", "API", "Media", "Sync", "Backup",
    "Temp", "Prod", "Dev"
]


def rand_ipv4_private(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose from private ranges with bias toward typical LANs
    choice = rng.choices(
        population=["192.168", "10", "172"],
        weights=[60, 25, 15],
        k=1
    )[0]
    if choice == "192.168":
        a, b, c, d = 192, 168, rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(2, 254)
    elif choice == "10":
        a, b, c, d = 10, rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(2, 254)
    else:  # 172.16.0.0/12
        a, b, c, d = 172, rng.randint(16, 31), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(2, 254)
    return f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"


def rand_ipv4_publicish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Avoid obvious reserved ranges; still not actually routed
    while True:
        a = rng.randint(1, 223)
        if a in (10, 127, 169, 172, 192):
            continue
        b, c, d = rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(0, 255), rng.randint(1, 254)
        ip = f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"
        try:
            ipaddress.IPv4Address(ip)
            return ip
        except Exception:
            continue


def rand_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    label1 = rng.choice(COMMON_HOST_LABELS)
    label2 = rng.choice(COMMON_HOST_LABELS) if rng.random() < 0.4 else str(rng.randint(1, 9999))
    tld = rng.choice(COMMON_TLDS)
    name = f"{label1}-{label2}.{tld}"
    # Ensure <=63 chars
    return name[:63]


def rand_desc(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose 2-4 words plus port/proto hints, keep <=63
    words = rng.sample(DESC_WORDS, rng.randint(2, 4))
    suffix = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        suffix.append(rng.choice(["TCP", "UDP"]))
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        suffix.append(str(rng.randint(1, 65535)))
    desc = " ".join(words + suffix)
    if not desc:
        desc = "UPnP Mapping"
    return desc[:63]


def maybe_empty_remote(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 50% empty (wildcard), else hostname/IP
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return ""
    return rng.choice([rand_hostname(rng), rand_ipv4_publicish(rng)])[:63]


def pack_c_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated strings
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        out += s.encode('ascii', 'ignore') + b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # inClient must be IPv4 string; bias to private
    in_client = rand_ipv4_private(rng) if rng.random() < 0.85 else rand_ipv4_publicish(rng)

    # desc optional in stub, but provide a useful one
    desc = rand_desc(rng)

    # remoteHost: empty or host/ip
    remote = maybe_empty_remote(rng)

    # Provide a few extra strings to satisfy any additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls
    extras = []
    # Extra IPv4 candidates
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        extras.append(rand_ipv4_private(rng))
    # Extra descriptions
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        extras.append(rand_desc(rng))
    # Extra remote host variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        extras.append(maybe_empty_remote(rng))

    strings = [in_client, desc, remote] + extras
    blob = pack_c_strings(strings)

    # Ensure size limit
    return blob[:4096]

# This generator produces bytes that, when interpreted as a UTF-8 string by FUZZ_PARAM_STR

LABEL_MAX = 63


def _rand_ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Avoid multicast/invalid extremes sometimes, but also include edge cases
    choices = [
        "0.0.0.0", "255.255.255.255", "127.0.0.1", "1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8",
        f"{rng.randint(1, 223)}.{rng.randint(0,255)}.{rng.randint(0,255)}.{rng.randint(1,254)}",
    ]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _rand_ipv6(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    edge = [
        "::", "::1", "fe80::1", "2001:db8::1", "::ffff:192.0.2.128",
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(edge)
    # random global unicast-ish
    parts = [f"{rng.randrange(0, 0x10000):x}" for _ in range(8)]
    addr = ":".join(parts)
    # Occasionally compress
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        try:
            addr = str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(addr))
        except Exception:
            pass
    return addr


def _rand_port(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include common ports and boundaries
    candidates = ["0", "1", "53", "80", "123", "443", "1900", "5351", "65535"]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        candidates.append(str(rng.randint(0, 65535)))
    return rng.choice(candidates)


def _rand_proto_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return "TCP" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "UDP"


def _rand_proto_number(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For WANIPv6FirewallControl pinhole proto field (IP protocol numbers)
    proto_nums = ["6", "17", "1", "58", "255"]  # TCP, UDP, ICMP, ICMPv6, wildcard-ish
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        proto_nums.append(str(rng.randint(0, 255)))
    return rng.choice(proto_nums)


def _rand_hostname_label(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=LABEL_MAX) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, min(max_len, 16))
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(HOST_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # ensure label doesn't start/end with hyphen per hostname rules
    if s[0] == '-':
        s = 'a' + s[1:]
    if s[-1] == '-':
        s = s[:-1] + 'a'
    return s


def _rand_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create domain with 1-4 labels, include TLD variety and optional trailing dot
    tlds = ["local", "lan", "home", "com", "net", "org", "example"]
    labels = [_rand_hostname_label(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))]
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        labels[-1] = rng.choice(tlds)
    host = ".".join(labels)
    if rng.random() < 0.1:

def _rand_client_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # inClient expects internal IPv4 typically; provide a mix of IPv4, hostnames, and IPv6 (for pinholes)
    choices = [
        _rand_ipv4(rng),
        _rand_hostname(rng),
        _rand_ipv6(rng),

    # Bias towards IPv4 for port mapping APIs
    weights = [0.6, 0.25, 0.15]
    pick = rng.choices(choices, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    return pick[:63]


def _rand_remote_host(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Allow empty string for wildcard as many IGDs expect ""
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return ""
    # Otherwise provide hostname or IP (v4/v6), trimmed to 63
    return rng.choice([_rand_hostname(rng), _rand_ipv4(rng), _rand_ipv6(rng)])[:63]


def _rand_desc(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Human-friendly description, <=63
    base = rng.choice([
        "miniupnpc", "test mapping", "fuzz case", "service", "game server",
        "vpn", "web", "dns", "ntp", "ssh", "rdp"
    ])
    suffix = str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
    desc = f"{base}-{suffix}"
    return desc[:63]


def _rand_lease(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 0..604800 inclusive, include common durations
    common = [0, 60, 300, 3600, 86400, 604800]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        val = rng.choice(common)
    else:

# We build a compact TLV-like stream of multiple candidate strings separated with NULs so the fuzzer can
# pull distinct values. We include a variety of IPv6 forms, hostnames, and numeric strings. The total

TEMPL_HOSTNAMES = [
    "example.com",
    "gateway.local",
    "router.home",
    "xn--bcher-kva.example",  # IDNA-like
    "sub.domain.example",

# Some valid IPv6 addresses, including compressed, IPv4-mapped, and with zone index placeholders.
BASE_IPV6 = [
    "::1",
    "2001:db8::1",
    "2001:db8:0:1:2:3:4:5",

def rand_ipv6(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly choose to synthesize or pick from BASE_IPV6
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        base = rnd.choice(BASE_IPV6)
    else:
        # Generate random global unicast 2001:db8::/32 documentation prefix to stay safe
        hextets = [0x2001, 0x0db8] + [rnd.randrange(0, 0x10000) for _ in range(6)]
        base = ":".join(f"{h:x}" for h in hextets)
        try:
            base = ipaddress.IPv6Address(base).compressed
        except Exception:
            base = "2001:db8::1"
    # Optionally add scope for link-local addresses
    if base.startswith("fe80::") and rnd.random() < 0.7:
        scope = rnd.choice(SCOPES)
        base = f"{base}%{scope}"
    return base


def rand_hostname(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose from templates or synthesize a plausible hostname
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return rnd.choice(TEMPL_HOSTNAMES)
    # synthesize labels
    labels = []

    for _ in range(nlabels):

        # ensure no leading/trailing hyphen for hostname labels

def rand_port_str(rnd: random.Random) -> str:

    return str(rnd.randrange(0, 65536))


def rand_proto_strnum(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common protocol numbers for IPv6 pinholes, plus wildcard 65535
    choices = ["6", "17", "58", "132", "65535"]
    return rnd.choice(choices)


def rand_duration(rnd: random.Random) -> str:

    return str(rnd.randrange(0, 604801))


def rand_internal_client(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Could be IPv6 literal or hostname; ensure non-empty
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        return rand_ipv6(rnd)
    else:
        return rand_hostname(rnd)


def build_fields(rnd: random.Random) -> list[str]:
    fields = []

    # remoteHost candidates: empty (wildcard), IPv6, hostname
    fields.append("")
    fields.append(rand_ipv6(rnd))
    fields.append(rand_hostname(rnd))

    # remotePort and intPort candidates as decimal strings
    for _ in range(3):
        fields.append(rand_port_str(rnd))

    # internal client non-empty
    for _ in range(2):
        fields.append(rand_internal_client(rnd))

    # protocol number strings
    for _ in range(2):
        fields.append(rand_proto_strnum(rnd))

    # lease time options
    for _ in range(2):
        fields.append(rand_duration(rnd))

    # Also include literal TCP/UDP strings since one stub uses them
    fields.append("TCP")
    fields.append("UDP")

    # Add a few short random strings to cover trimming behavior (<=63 chars)
    for _ in range(3):
        l = rnd.randint(1, 63)
        s = ''.join(rnd.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-%') for _ in range(l))
        fields.append(s)

    # Ensure some IPv6 with scope variants are present
    fields.append("fe80::1%eth0")
    fields.append("fe80::abcd:1%3")

    return fields


def pack_null_separated(fields: list[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join fields with NUL separators; include a leading count header for potential consumers
    blob = bytearray()
    blob.extend(struct.pack('>I', len(fields)))
    for s in fields:
        # enforce max element size to keep total under limit
        bs = s.encode('utf-8')[:256]
        blob.extend(bs)
        blob.append(0)
    return bytes(blob[:MAX_SIZE])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    fields = build_fields(rnd)
    rnd.shuffle(fields)
    data = pack_null_separated(fields)
    return data

    fields: List[Tuple[str, str]] = [

        ("NewProtocol", proto),

        ("NewInternalClient", int_client),

    if rng.random() < 0.4:

    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        name, val = rng.choice(fields)
        if name in ("NewDescription", "NewRemoteHost"):
            alt = val + "-dup" if val else "dup"

            alt = _rand_lease(rng)

    mandatory = {"NewExternalPort", "NewProtocol", "NewInternalClient"}

def _wrap_listing(entries: List[str]) -> str:
    # The NewPortListing fragment is inside a SOAP envelope in real responses.
    # Provide a compact, valid envelope including namespaces often seen by parsers.
    body = "\n".join(entries)
    return (

        "<s:Envelope xmlns:s=\"http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/\"\n"
        "             s:encodingStyle=\"http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/\">\n"

        "      </NewPortListing>\n"
        "    </u:GetListOfPortMappingsResponse>\n"
        "  </s:Body>\n"
        "</s:Envelope>\n"
    )


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide number of entries; try to keep total size <= 4096
    n = rng.randint(0, 12)
    entries: List[str] = []

    # Ensure at least one valid minimal mapping sometimes
    if n == 0:

    for i in range(n):
        entries.append(_make_entry(rng, i))

    xml = _wrap_listing(entries)

    # If size exceeds 4096, reduce entries until within limit
    # Keep at least one entry
    while len(xml.encode('utf-8')) > 4096 and len(entries) > 1:
        entries.pop()
        xml = _wrap_listing(entries)

    return xml.encode("utf-8")

# Generator for XML element names suitable for IGDstartelt/IGDendelt handlers.
# These handlers receive (name, namelen). The fuzzing harness may pass namelen=0
# with name=NULL. When namelen>0, name must reference at least namelen bytes.
# We therefore produce a bytes buffer that contains plausible XML element names
# and various interesting cases concatenated together. The harness will slice
# from this buffer with arbitrary lengths, so the buffer should contain many
# valid tag-name substrings and edge cases.

XML_NAME_START_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + ':' + '_'
XML_NAME_CHARS = XML_NAME_START_CHARS + string.digits + '-' + '.'

COMMON_TAGS = [
    # IGD/UPnP device description related
    'root', 'device', 'service', 'serviceList', 'deviceList', 'URLBase',
    'friendlyName', 'manufacturer', 'modelName', 'UDN', 'SCPDURL',
    'controlURL', 'eventSubURL', 'serviceType', 'presentationURL',
    # WAN services
    'WANDevice', 'WANConnectionDevice', 'WANIPConnection', 'WANPPPConnection',
    'WANCommonInterfaceConfig', 'WANIPv6FirewallControl',
    # Port mapping related
    'PortMappingEntry', 'NewRemoteHost', 'NewExternalPort', 'NewProtocol',
    'NewInternalPort', 'NewInternalClient', 'NewEnabled', 'NewDescription',
    'NewLeaseTime', 'NewPortListing',
]

# Some namespace-like prefixes often seen in UPnP XML
NS_PREFIXES = ['urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:', 'urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:']


def rand_xml_name(rng: random.Random, maxlen: int = 64) -> str:
    # Generate a valid XML name of length 1..maxlen using allowed characters.
    n = rng.randint(1, maxlen)
    start = rng.choice(XML_NAME_START_CHARS)
    if n == 1:
        return start
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(XML_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return start + rest


def build_pool(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Include common tags in multiple casings and with typical prefixes
    for tag in COMMON_TAGS:
        parts.append(tag.encode('utf-8'))
        parts.append(tag.lower().encode('utf-8'))
        parts.append(tag.upper().encode('utf-8'))
        # With and without common IGD prefixes like urn service types (not strictly names but useful substrings)
        for prefix in NS_PREFIXES:
            combined = (prefix + tag + ':1')  # resembles service type
            parts.append(combined.encode('utf-8'))

    # 2) Random valid XML names of varying lengths including boundary sizes
    for L in [1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63]:
        name = rand_xml_name(rng, L)
        parts.append(name.encode('utf-8'))

    for _ in range(50):
        parts.append(rand_xml_name(rng, rng.randint(1, 64)).encode('utf-8'))

    # 3) Edge-case names: include colon and underscore, dash, dot variations
    edge_names = [
        'a', '_', 'A', 'Z', 'a-b', 'a.b', 'a_b', '_x1', 'ns:tag', 'upnp:service', 'x:1',
        'ServiceType', 'controlURL', 'eventSubURL', 'SCPDURL', 'URLBase',
    ]
    parts.extend(s.encode('utf-8') for s in edge_names)

    # 4) Include some zero bytes between names so that slicing with arbitrary length
    # can expose shorter names and names with embedded NUL tails (handler uses length).
    inter_spacers = [b'\x00', b'\x00\x00', b'\x00'*4]

    out = bytearray()
    # Start with a short valid token for namelen small values
    out.extend(b'device')

    # Interleave parts and spacers, and add separators like '>' '/' which are common around names
    seps = [b'', b'>', b'/>', b'</', b' ']

    for p in parts:
        out.extend(rng.choice(seps))
        out.extend(p)
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            out.extend(rng.choice(inter_spacers))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            # Append a typical end/start delimiter; handlers ignore it but it helps create diverse slices
            out.extend(rng.choice(seps))

    # 5) Ensure buffer length stays within 4096 bytes
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    # Guarantee not empty
    if not out:
        out.extend(b'root')

    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_pool(rng)

def _rand_url(r: random.Random) -> str:

    return f"http://[{ipv6}{scope}]{path}"

# Common XML character data that the IGD device description parser is interested in
_SERVICE_TYPES = [
    "urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:1",
    "urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:WANIPConnection:2",

def _random_visible_text(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)

    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _cdata_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    v: List[bytes] = []

    # URLs that could appear as controlurl/eventsuburl/scpdurl/presentationURL
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        v.append(_rand_url(r).encode("utf-8"))

    # URLBase and presentationURL may be absolute or relative
    v.append(b"/")
    v.append(b"//router.local/")

    # Service types
    for s in _SERVICE_TYPES:
        v.append(s.encode("ascii"))

    # Short tokens likely to be copied into fixed-size buffers
    v.extend([
        b"TCP", b"UDP", b"IP_Routed", b"IP_Bridged", b"Unconfigured",
    ])

    # IPv4/IPv6 addresses
    v.append(_rand_ipv4(r).encode("ascii"))
    v.append(_rand_ipv6(r).encode("ascii"))

    # Longish paths to exercise truncation boundaries (typical MINIUPNPC_URL_MAXSIZE is 128/256)
    long_path = "/" + ("a" * r.randint(60, 240))
    v.append(long_path.encode("ascii"))

    # Random visible text chunks with spaces and punctuation
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        v.append(_random_visible_text(r, 1, r.randint(8, 64)).encode("utf-8"))

    # Whitespace-only chunks, including mixed whitespace
    v.extend([b" ", b"\t\t", b"\n", b"\r\n\t "])

    # Empty string (datalen may be 0, but having empty with non-zero len is also useful)
    v.append(b"")

    # CDATA-like sequences and XML-escaped entities that could be delivered as character data
    v.extend([b"&", b"<", b">", b"<![CDATA[some text]]>"])

    # Non-ASCII UTF-8 text to ensure handler accepts arbitrary bytes
    v.extend([
        "Презентация".encode("utf-8"),
        "表示".encode("utf-8"),
        "présentation".encode("utf-8"),
    ])

    # Boundary-size strings near typical limits (63/64/127/128/255)
    for n in [63, 64, 127, 128, 255]:
        v.append(("x" * n).encode("ascii"))

    return v

def _compose_stream(r: random.Random, chunks: List[bytes], budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a stream by concatenating a selection of chunks and random fillers, up to budget bytes
    out = bytearray()
    # Start with a likely URL/service type to simulate realistic data burst
    prefix = r.choice(chunks)
    if len(prefix) <= budget:
        out.extend(prefix)
    # Then interleave random chosen chunks and small random strings
    while len(out) < budget and r.random() < 0.95:
        choice = r.choice(chunks)
        # Occasionally add small random filler
        if r.random() < 0.35:
            filler = _random_visible_text(r, 0, 12).encode("utf-8")
            piece = filler
        else:
            piece = choice
        # Add optional whitespace around pieces
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            piece = b" " + piece
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            piece = piece + b"\n"
        if len(out) + len(piece) > budget:
            piece = piece[: max(0, budget - len(out))]
        out.extend(piece)
        if len(out) >= budget or r.random() < 0.08:
            break
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Select an intended semantic to bias the content
    mode = r.choice([
        "service", "url", "addr", "mixed", "whitespace", "longpath",
    ])

    chunks = _cdata_variants(r)

    # Budget for the resulting buffer, cap at 1024 to remain small yet expressive
    if mode == "whitespace":
        budget = r.randint(0, 64)  # allow empty delivery and tiny whitespace bursts
    elif mode == "longpath":
        budget = r.randint(64, 512)
    else:
        budget = r.randint(8, 512)

    # Bias initial chunk list according to the mode
    if mode == "service":
        chunks.extend(s.encode("ascii") for s in _SERVICE_TYPES)
    elif mode == "url":
        chunks.extend(_rand_url(r).encode("utf-8") for _ in range(3))
    elif mode == "addr":
        chunks.extend([_rand_ipv4(r).encode("ascii"), _rand_ipv6(r).encode("ascii")])

    payload = _compose_stream(r, chunks, budget)

    # Ensure overall size constraint per instructions
    return payload[:4096]

# Helper to XML-escape text occasionally with entities
def maybe_escape(text: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if not text:
        return text
    # randomly decide to escape some characters
    s = []
    for ch in text:
        if rnd.random() < 0.25:
            if ch in dict(XML_ENTITIES):
                s.append(dict(XML_ENTITIES)[ch])
            else:
                s.append(ch)
        else:
            s.append(ch)
    return "".join(s)

# Build an element with optional namespace prefix and CDATA wrapping
def build_element(name: str, value: str, ns_prefix: str | None, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # sometimes use CDATA if value has special chars
    use_cdata = rnd.random() < 0.20 and (any(c in value for c in "&<>\"") or rnd.random() < 0.3)
    content = f"<![CDATA[{value}]]>" if use_cdata else maybe_escape(value, rnd)
    qname = f"{ns_prefix}:{name}" if ns_prefix else name
    # optional whitespace variations
    space_inside = " " if rnd.random() < 0.2 else ""
    return f"<{qname}{space_inside}>{content}</{qname}>"

# Compose a SOAP envelope with action response and various fields
def build_soap(action: str, args: List[Tuple[str, List[str]]], rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # choose SOAP version and prefixes
    soap_ns = SOAP_ENVELOPE_NS12 if rnd.random() < 0.3 else SOAP_ENVELOPE_NS
    senv = "s" if rnd.random() < 0.5 else "soap"
    supnp = "u"

    # choose a service type
    service = rnd.choice([WANIP_V1, WANIP_V2, WANCOMMON_V1])

    # namespaces on Envelope
    ns_attrs = [
        f"xmlns:{senv}=\"{soap_ns}\"",
        f"xmlns:{supnp}=\"{UPNP_CONTROL_NS}\"",
        f"xmlns:svc=\"{service}\"",
    ]
    # Include encodingStyle occasionally
    if rnd.random() < 0.25:
        ns_attrs.append(f"{senv}:encodingStyle=\"http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/\"")

    # Optional XML declaration and leading/trailing whitespace or comments
    parts = []
    if rnd.random() < 0.8:
        enc = rnd.choice(["utf-8", "utf-16", "iso-8859-1"]) if rnd.random() < 0.1 else "utf-8"
        parts.append(f"<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"{enc}\"?>")
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append("<!-- UPnP SOAP response generated -->")

    parts.append(f"<{senv}:Envelope {' '.join(ns_attrs)}>")
    parts.append(f"  <{senv}:Body>")

    # Action response element can be namespaced by u: or svc:
    resp_prefix = rnd.choice([supnp, "svc", None])
    attr_servicetype = f" {supnp}:serviceType=\"{service}\"" if rnd.random() < 0.5 else ""

    # open action response
    qname = f"{resp_prefix}:{action}" if resp_prefix else action
    parts.append(f"    <{qname}{attr_servicetype}>")

    # mix in provided args, with optional duplicates and extra irrelevant elements
    for (arg_name, choices) in args:
        # 1 to 3 occurrences to test duplicates/last-wins behavior
        reps = 1 + int(rnd.random() < 0.35) + int(rnd.random() < 0.15)
        for _ in range(reps):
            val = rnd.choice(choices)
            parts.append("      " + build_element(arg_name, val, None if rnd.random() < 0.3 else supnp, rnd))
        # sometimes insert filler/unknown element
        if rnd.random() < 0.25:
            filler_name = rnd.choice(["Foo", "Bar", "Result", "Error", "X"])
            filler_val = rnd.choice(["0", "1", "OK", "NOK", "unused"]) 
            parts.append("      " + build_element(filler_name, filler_val, None, rnd))

    # add some common name/value pairs outside the action as others might parse
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append("      " + build_element("URLBase", rnd.choice(["http://192.0.2.1:49000/", "http://[fe80::1%25eth0]/"]), "svc", rnd))

    parts.append(f"    </{qname}>")
    parts.append(f"  </{senv}:Body>")
    parts.append(f"</{senv}:Envelope>")

    xml = "\n".join(parts)

    # Optionally wrap in extra whitespace or BOM-like leading chars (but keep UTF-8 bytes)
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        xml = "\n\n" + xml + "\n"
    return xml

# Select an action set to generate a variety of valid responses
def pick_action_set(rnd: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, List[Tuple[str, List[str]]]]:
    # mix common and IPv6 firewall responses
    pools = [ACTION_RESPONSES]
    if rnd.random() < 0.25:
        pools.append(IPV6_FC_RESPONSES)
    pool = {}
    for p in pools:
        pool.update(p)
    action = rnd.choice(list(pool.keys()))
    return action, pool[action]

# Truncate to limits and ensure <= 4096 bytes
def clamp_size(b: bytes, limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    if len(b) <= limit:
        return b
    # Try to cut at a closing tag boundary to preserve well-formedness
    cut = b.rfind(b">", 0, limit)
    if cut == -1:
        return b[:limit]
    return b[:cut+1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose between 1 and 3 concatenated SOAP responses to test parser's handling of extra data
    count = 1 + rnd.randrange(3)
    docs = []
    for _ in range(count):
        action, args = pick_action_set(rnd)
        xml = build_soap(action, args, rnd)
        docs.append(xml)
        # Optionally append a second related action in same buffer to encourage multi-pair parsing
        if rnd.random() < 0.35:
            a2, args2 = pick_action_set(rnd)
            docs.append(build_soap(a2, args2, rnd))

    # Join with some whitespace or minimal noise that remains valid XML between docs
    sep = "\n\n" if rnd.random() < 0.7 else "\n<!-- next -->\n"
    payload = sep.join(docs)

    # Guarantee non-empty and within size constraint
    data = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    data = clamp_size(data, 4096)
    if not data:
        # Fallback minimal valid SOAP
        minimal = (
            "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?>\n"
            "<s:Envelope xmlns:s=\"http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/\" xmlns:u=\"urn:schemas-upnp-org:control-1-0\">\n"
            "  <s:Body>\n"
            "    <u:GetStatusInfoResponse>\n"
            "      <NewConnectionStatus>Connected</NewConnectionStatus>\n"
            "      <NewLastConnectionError>ERROR_NONE</NewLastConnectionError>\n"
            "      <NewUptime>0</NewUptime>\n"
            "    </u:GetStatusInfoResponse>\n"
            "  </s:Body>\n"
            "</s:Envelope>\n"
        ).encode("utf-8")
        return minimal
    return data
